title: a far bus handle's flush answers without asking the LAN door for an op it refuses
intention: RemoteBus.flush() on a far home sends nothing and answers that the ring belongs to the far box's bus process; on a local home it still sends op flush.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 from akienasus (CAIRN_BUS_HOME on akiendelllinux): each bin/cairn test --seal printed "'flush' is not open across the LAN" and 'the crossings they would have fired did not', yet all 12 tester->codemother sealed posts were in her channel and her sealed replies came back accepted:true. The post rides op call and her hook runs in the far bus process; only the trailing flush, an op the LAN door refuses by design (Law 6), raised, and the tester reported a failure that did not happen.
traces_to: Law 7 (a diagnostic surface may not report a failure that did not happen) and Law 6 (the far ring is its own box's process to flush; server.py LAN_OPS).
how: In RemoteBus.flush (cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py): when self._far is not None return {'flushed': 0, 'receipts': 0, 'far': 'host:port', 'why': ...} and send nothing; otherwise send op flush as now. Red-first proof replacing remote.exchange, as test_a_far_client_reaches_without_hold.py does, LAN_OPS restated.

clauses.claim: with a far home, RemoteBus.flush() sends no request and returns a dict carrying flushed 0, far naming host:port, and a non-empty why
with a far home, a post followed by flush sends only ops in ('call','stats','verbs')
with a local home, flush() still sends exactly one op flush

decisions.text: D1: RemoteBus.flush answers a far home without an op; a local home is unchanged.
D2: the proof, one tooth per clause, with remote.exchange replaced so nothing dials.
